Event queue admission overflow handling wait waking and shutdown sequencing.

findings.text: Default encrypted IO policy helpers always permit bio merging, return the requested block count unchanged, and report zeroing as unsupported.
Link rename readdir setattr and symlink encryption preparation act as encrypted state gates that delegate to specialized handlers when encryption applies and otherwise succeed immediately.

Lookup preparation for plain directories clears the name object, aliases user and disk views to the dentry name and length, flags the dentry as plain, and succeeds, while encrypted directories take a different path.
Error reporting uses a deferred container with work linkage, superblock, optional inode, byte offset and length, categorized type, and negative error code.

Inline error reporters forward to a shared routine with preset arguments for generic IO, data loss with IO failure, file metadata at zero range, superblock metadata without inode, and shutdown with shutdown error.
Error categories are ordered as buffered read, buffered write, direct read, direct write, data lost, then metadata.

Memory map permission checks have a permissive build that always succeeds and a filtering build that succeeds for missing files or non HSM modes and otherwise consults pre content notification for the range.
Rmdir notification must not run on a negative dentry and warns once then skips in that case, otherwise it reports deletion with parent, child inode and dentry.

Base event bits are access 0x1, modify 0x2, attrib 0x4, close write 0x8, close nowrite 0x10, open 0x20, moved from 0x40, moved to 0x80, create 0x100, delete 0x200, delete self 0x400, move self 0x800, open exec 0x1000, unmount 0x2000, queue overflow 0x4000, with error and ignored sharing 0x8000.

Permission and mount bits are open perm 0x10000, access perm 0x20000, open exec perm 0x40000, pre access 0x100000, mount attach 0x1000000 and detach 0x2000000, with mount move as attach combined with detach.

Structural markers are event on child 0x8000000, rename 0x10000000, multishot 0x20000000 and isdir 0x40000000, with move as moved from combined with moved to; dirent aggregate combines create delete move rename, mount aggregate combines attach detach, content perm combines three perm bits, pre content is pre access alone, and all perm combines content and pre content.

Child possible events combine all perm events with access modify attrib both close kinds open and open exec; parent possible equals child possible; global events add dirent mount child possible delete self move self unmount overflow ignored and error; flag aggregate combines isdir event on child multishot and full bits combine events with flags.
Group option bits are user allocated 0x01 and duplicate marks allowed 0x02.

Connector flags are watched 0x01 and has reference 0x02; mark flags are alive 0x1 attached 0x2 excl unlink 0x10 oneshot 0x20 ignored survives modify 0x100 no reference 0x200 has ignore flags 0x400 has fsid 0x800 and weak fsid 0x1000.
Group behavior is supplied through callbacks for generic event dispatch, inode event dispatch, group private release, mark lifecycle stages, and event release with final mark freeing.
The common event header contains only queue linkage for embedding in larger backend events.
Group priority ranks normal first, content permission second and pre content third, followed by a count sentinel.

A group bundles operations, reference count, queue lock list wait queue length limit priority and shutdown state, option flags with saved allocation state, mark mutex wait count and mark list, async notification, overflow placeholder, resource accounting, and a private union for inotify or fanotify state including identifiers merge structures access waiting and pools.

Notification queue mutation is serialized by a spinlock, while mark list work requires the group mutex held with filesystem reclaim disabled across the critical section, with an assertion that warns unless both conditions hold.

Payload variants include an error report with code inode and superblock, a file range with path offset and length, a mount reference with namespace and identifier, and rename data with moved dentry and optional overwritten inode, discriminated by a tag covering none file range path inode dentry mount error and rename.

Typed payload extractors return the matching view for inode dentry path superblock mount mount identifier error report rename target and file range, and yield null or zero when the discriminator does not provide that view.

Traversal slots enumerate inode, vfsmount, superblock, parent, second inode, mount namespace and count; object kinds add wildcard any, the four concrete kinds with count, and a detached alias equal to count, where validity means strictly below count.

Iteration state keeps one mark per slot plus current group, a bitmask of reportable slots and an RCU index; helpers test or set slot bits, return a mark only when its bit is set, and advance to the next reportable slot, with macros to walk all slots or only reported marks.
A connector joins one watched object to its marks with type, highest priority, option flags, an object pointer shared with deferred teardown linkage, and a mark list.

Connector type priority flags object pointer and mark list are guarded by the connector spinlock; superblock connector lists use a dedicated list lock; mark masks flags and attachment pointers are guarded by the mark spinlock with mask and ignore mask also requiring the group mutex.

Superblock tracking holds an RCU superblock connector, a list of inode connectors, and per priority watched object counters where slot zero totals everything and each higher slot counts objects watched at that priority or above; a helper exposes the total counter.

A mark carries its mask, reference count, owning group, group linkage shared with teardown queueing, object linkage and connector, ignore mask and flag word for alive attached and backend specific behaviors.
Setting shutdown blocks further queueing; queue depth is limited by current length against a maximum with a reserved overflow event for the full condition.
Group lifetime is reference driven where the final drop reclaims all resources; some groups pin the count permanently while descriptor backed groups release when the descriptor closes.
Headers use include guards to ensure single inclusion.
